priority.override_reason: Rank-one controlflow-recursive remains dominated by the closed direct-leaf/frame and generic-dispatch mechanisms. The rank-two A* profile independently exposes a current storage threshold: every GraphNode gains a ninth ordinary data field, which moves it from the retained small vector to a per-instance dynamic name map and makes the existing shared small-slot cache unavailable. This is a storage-policy change, not a constructor shape or cache-layout retry.

mechanism.summary: Keep ordinary objects with at most twelve string properties in the existing compact linear storage, so repeated 9-to-12-field receivers can retain the established shared data-slot cache instead of immediately allocating a dynamic name map.
mechanism.generality: Selection depends only on the live count of ordinary own string properties. It does not inspect constructors, function names, bytecode identity, source paths, benchmark names, arguments, iteration counts, or results. Objects that grow past twelve fields retain the current dynamic map behavior, and every property lookup, descriptor operation, deletion, extensibility, and enumeration path continues to use the same storage API.
semantic_risks: preserving ECMAScript own-property insertion order and array-index ordering across the later small-to-dynamic promotion
preserving descriptor, accessor, writable, configurable, delete, and non-extensible behavior while the object remains in the larger small-storage range
ensuring shared named-property slots retain their interned-key and data-descriptor checks after ordinary value writes
